If AACommServer was closed unexpectedly the string is AACommServerNotRunning. Suppressed only when a SendReceive(AACommMessage) was in flight AND no concurrent async Send(AACommMessage) was in flight (sync caller observes via the SR return; mixed-mode fatals still fire). Invoked synchronously on the transport receiver thread — off-load long work via Task.Run. Do NOT call API functions from the handler; no Disconnect needed after. public event Action OnCommsError Event Type Action OnLongOperationEnded Fired when a long controller operation (Reset, Save, Load, SaveUser, EventCorrect) ends. Parameters: identifying the operation, and the controller error code — 0 means no error (the operation succeeded); a non-zero value is the controller error code (e.g. 22 = "motor on"), or an unresolved-error sentinel when the operation ended without a parseable reply (e.g. session teardown). Fired only if the matching fired: a long op whose reply lands within the start-grace window raises neither edge (see ). Do NOT call API functions while handling. Event is invoked in a new Task. Event NOT invoked if method is used. For Reset: NOT invoked if the Reset reply was an error, if reconnecting after reset failed, or if the API was disconnected while in reset progress. public event Action OnLongOperationEnded Event Type Action OnLongOperationStarted Fired when a long controller operation (Reset, Save, Load, SaveUser, EventCorrect) begins. Parameter: identifying the operation. For Save/Load/SaveUser/EventCorrect: NOT fired when the controller replies within a short start-grace window — such a reply means the op was not long-running (e.g. an immediate ERR 22 rejecting a flash Save while the motor is on), and the reply surfaces its own result; the matching is suppressed too. Do NOT call API functions while handling. Event is invoked in a new Task. Event NOT invoked if method is used. public event Action OnLongOperationStarted Event Type Action OnPushMessageReceived Raised when an unsolicited "push" message is received from the controller. The event delivers a parsed AACommPushMsgBase instance (created by AACommPushMsgBase.Parse) and is invoked on a background Task to avoid blocking the receiver thread. Handlers should be aware that multiple push messages may be received in quick succession, so code re-entry and thread-safety should be considered. public event Action OnPushMessageReceived Event Type Action OnUserUnitsEnabledChanged Raised after the controller confirms (OK reply) a per-axis User Units enable/disable change, regardless of the path that sent it (API, Terminal, …). Fires only on an actual transition. The cache behind GetUserUnitsEnabled(char) is updated synchronously on the receiver thread before this fires, so handlers should re-read it rather than rely on event ordering. Invoked on a background Task (like OnPushMessageReceived); consider re-entrancy and thread-safety. Args: (axis, isEnabled). public event Action OnUserUnitsEnabledChanged Event Type Action

api/AAComm.Services.Diagnostics.AACommDe.title: Class AACommDebugLog | Agito AAComm SDK
api/AAComm.Services.Diagnostics.AACommDe.summary: Class AACommDebugLog Namespace AAComm.Services.Diagnostics Assembly AAComm.dll Process-wide, zero-config, always-on diagnostic log for the AAComm client — the client-side counterpart of AACommServer's debug log. Session-lifecycle events (construction, connect outcomes, sync-timeout expiries, FATALs, disconnects) accumulate in an in-memory ring; healthy steady state does zero file IO. A severe event (sync phase-2 teardown, FATAL, comms error) snapshots the ring to %LocalAppData%\PCSuite\AAComm_DebugLogs{yyyy_MM_dd_HH-mm-ss}{process}{pid}_{trigger}.log off the hot path (debounced, 5 s), because a library in the customer's process has no reliable exit hook to save on. Never per-message traffic — that is the AACommServer comm log's job. Every line is tagged HH:mm:ss.fff [api#N/conn#M] text: api#N identifies the CommAPI instance, conn#M its successive channel opens; the connect line carries the full endpoint (and the socket's local port, which AACommServer's log can join against its per-client UserId). public static class AACommDebugLog Inheritance object AACommDebugLog Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Properties Sink Optional host bridge: receives each event line as (source, formatted line), where source is the line's identity tag — api#N or api#N/conn#M, and on the connect line the tag also carries →endpoint, so hosts routing on source should prefix-match. The one-time process header line is ring-only and does not reach the sink. Mirrors AACommServer's GlobalLogger.GlobalDebugLog; lets a host forward AAComm diagnostics into its own session log. Invoked synchronously on the logging thread — keep handlers cheap. public static Action<string, string> Sink { get; set; } Property Value Action<string, string> Methods Flush() Writes the current in-memory ring to a timestamped snapshot file NOW (synchronously), without clearing it. Never throws; healthy processes may call this on demand. public static void Flush()

These are written only through the User Units API (ControllerMessagesContainer.TrySetUnitsSync): the units name is a multi-write char array whose adapter cache can't be kept correct by sniffing single raw writes, so raw assignments to them are rejected by the Tx-build gate. The read-only group array (GroupSuffix) and the event-driven enable parameter (UserUnitsEn) are deliberately NOT included. public static bool IsUserUnitsConfig(string mnemonic) Parameters mnemonic string Returns bool MessageAssignsUserUnitsConfig(string) Returns whether a full controller message (single axis prefix + mnemonic + optional [index] + assignment), e.g. "APosUnitFct=0.5" or "BPosUnitUnt[3]=109", assigns a User Units config parameter (see IsUserUnitsConfig(string)). Queries (no '='/',') return false. Provisioning tools use this to decide whether a bulk write needs a post-write CommAPI.RefreshUserUnits to resync the scaling cache the raw write left stale. public static bool MessageAssignsUserUnitsConfig(string message) Parameters message string Returns bool TryParseUserUnitsEnAssignment(string, out char, out bool) Detects a single-axis UserUnitsEn assignment, e.g. "AUserUnitsEn=1" or "BUserUnitsEn,0". Returns false for queries (no '='/',') and for any other mnemonic. Used on the reply path to keep the enabled cache ack-authoritative and to fire the change event. Single-char axis prefix only. public static bool TryParseUserUnitsEnAssignment(string message, out char axis, out bool enabled) Parameters message string the sent message (axis + mnemonic + assignment) axis char resolved upper-cased axis char when the method returns true enabled bool the assigned state (value != "0") when the method returns true Returns bool

The version floor CLASSIFIES the attach, it never rejects: a legacy server still connects (compat mode), because a new client must coexist with a server started by an older SDK application on the same machine — but the degraded mode is queryable here instead of silent. A client must never shut down a server it did not spawn. public enum ServerCompat Fields Current = 1 Binary server at or above the client's floor — full feature set (correlated reply routing, channel events, version-gated features). LegacyAscii = 3 ASCII-only server: arrival-order reply routing, no channel events. The client's ASCII pipeline is frozen (deprecated) and kept solely for this compat mode. LegacyBinary = 2 Binary server below the floor (or reporting no parseable version): correlated routing works, but features behind newer version gates silently skip. Dormant while the floor equals the typed-payloads shipping version — a pre-typed binary server fails the handshake gate and attaches as ASCII (LegacyAscii); this value becomes reachable again at the next floor raise, for older-but-typed servers. Unknown = 0 Not connected (or connection not yet classified).

articles/advanced/firmware-download.html.title: Firmware Download | Agito AAComm SDK
articles/advanced/firmware-download.html.summary: Firmware & FPGA Download Overview Firmware (and, for non-AGM800 products, FPGA) images download over Ethernet or RS-232 — never CAN (see Transport support). AGM800 binary (.bin) firmware is validated via embedded magic markers and an optional .ver file, at parity with the non-AGM800 (.hex FW + .dat FPGA) products. Transport support FW download runs over Ethernet (AGM800 family — Ethernet only) or RS-232 (non-AGM800 products). It is NOT supported over CAN — AACommDownloadFW (StartDownloading/StartDownloadingSafe) rejects a CAN ConnectionData up front with "Firmware download is not supported over CAN…". The controller's CAN boot-loader FW-data contract is owned by the C2000 flash kernel at 0x100000 (separate from the application image) and is not met by this client path, so a CAN attempt fails controller-side with ERR 43 (unexpected character) / ERR 15 (unexpected byte count). Use Ethernet or RS-232. The AGD301 FW (.hex) and FPGA (.dat) download paths are HW-validated over RS-232 on both the String and Binary IPC protocols (Agd301HardwareTests, goldens AGD301orAGC301_2D05_V3.0.42.hex + AGD301_for_BissC_and_SinCos_v2.7.2.dat). FPGA download requires normal mode — it rejects BOOT. The complete gate matrix per download path — product, transport, exact-address and subnet rules, boot mode, file targets, version compatibility — with the CI-rig consequences is docs/ci-cd/fw-fpga-download-constraints.md. Backward Compatibility No .ver file: AGM800 firmware download proceeds without validation (same behavior as before) .ver file exists: Performs MD5 checksum, version, and product type validation before download Binary Firmware Parsing (AACommBinFwInfo) Parses Zynq binary firmware files to extract identity and version information using magic markers embedded in the binary. Magic Markers Each marker starts with the signature "AKRB" followed by a type tag: Marker Tag Payload Identity IDNT version(4) + size(4) + int32[32] (128 bytes) Version VERS version(4) + size(4) + char[4][64] (256 bytes) Byte-order note: Marker types are stored as little-endian 32-bit integers. "IDNT" (0x49444E54) appears as bytes 54 4E 44 49 ("TNDI" in a hex editor). Similarly, "VERS" appears as "SREV". Extracted Identity Data (32 int32 values) Index Field 0 Data version 1 Product type 2-6 FW version: Major.Minor.Patch.Owner-Subversion 7 Continuous current limit 8 Peak current limit 9 Number of axes 17 Full scale current 31 Magic end marker (0x12345678) .ver File Format (AGM800) Line 1: Version (optional) e.g. "3.8.0.0-123" Line 2: MD5 (optional) e.g. "MD5:XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX-XX" Line 3: Type (optional) e.g. "Type:AGM800" Valid Type values: AGM800, CiG1-MAS02, MAS02 Validation Steps (when .ver file exists) MD5 checksum verification (if MD5: line present) Version match between .ver and binary identity data (if binary contains identity markers) Product type validation (if Type: line present) — two independent checks: Binary identity: AGM800 family product-type IDs (6=AGM400, 10=AGM800, 15=PULSE_SYNC) are considered compatible Type string: only AGM800, CiG1-MAS02, MAS02 are accepted. Note: Pulse-Sync is NOT a valid Type string even though product type 15 passes the binary identity check MAS02 Hex-Encoding (IPC Framing Fix) MAS02 binary FW packets are raw binary that may contain 0x3E 0x0D — the IPC envelope terminator (>\r). To keep the IPC body ASCII-safe, the client wraps each binary chunk with the @#HEX: sigil (CommCommons.HexEncodedPrefix): <message-type-prefix>@#HEX:<hex-pairs>\r The server-side SocketMessageData detects the sigil via IndexOf, strips it, decodes the hex pairs back to raw bytes, and forwards a byte-identical payload to the controller. The per-packet MAS02 header and EOF marker are encoded as hex ASCII strings ("0000" / "FFFF") rather than raw char constants. This @#HEX: framing is the string-protocol path. Under the default binary (protobuf) IPC the raw FW bytes ride in IpcRequest.PayloadBytes with no hex round-trip — see architecture.md (IPC Framing). Post-Reset Disconnect Tolerance Both FW and FPGA download use ResetReplyHelper.IsExpectedPostResetDisconnect after the final packet/batch to handle the race where the controller resets before the OK reply arrives. Disconnect-style replies (ERR 4021, ERR 4020, channel-fatal) are accepted as success for the last step. Files Added: AACommComponents/AAComm/Extensions/AACommBinFwInfo.cs Modified: AACommComponents/AAComm/Extensions/AACommFwInfo.cs Constructor parses AGM800 .bin files via AACommBinFwInfo DataValid property: private setter ValidateFwFiles enhanced for AGM800 with optional .ver file ProductTypeStr returns "AGM800" for all AGM800 family types AACommComponents/AAComm/Extensions/AACommDownloadFW.cs MAS02 packets wrapped with @#HEX: sigil for IPC-safe binary transport TriageFwReply helper for post-reset disconnect tolerance AACommComponents/AAComm/Extensions/AACommDownloadFPGA.cs EOF reply uses ResetReplyHelper.IsExpectedPostResetDisconnect

articles/architecture/diagnostics.html.title: Diagnostic Debug Logs | Agito AAComm SDK
articles/architecture/diagnostics.html.summary: Diagnostic Debug Logs — client, server, and how they join The SDK's always-on diagnostic layer: what the AAComm client and AACommServer record about session lifecycle, where the files land, and the procedure that correlates the two logs for a single connection. This is the spec for the diagnostic logs only — the AACommServer comm log (per-channel message traffic, saved from the server UI) and PCSuite's Serilog session log (the PCSuite_DebugLogs sibling) are separate facilities. Design constraints Zero-config, always-on. AAComm runs inside customer processes; a diagnostic that must be enabled first never exists when the incident happens. Zero steady-state file IO. Entries accumulate in an in-memory ring; a healthy process never touches the disk. Only a severe event (or an explicit flush) writes a file. No per-message traffic. Message-level logging is the AACommServer comm log's job; the SendReceive/Send hot paths gain no logging on the success path. No wire change. The client↔server correlation works purely from what each side already sees on its own socket. Folder layout One folder per producer, all under %LocalAppData%\PCSuite\: Folder Producer Written when AAComm_DebugLogs\ AAComm client (AACommDebugLog) severe event or Flush() AACommServer_DebugLogs\ AACommServer (GlobalLogger); sniffer captures under Sniffer\ shutdown save, flush verb, implicit-shutdown save PCSuite_DebugLogs\ PCSuite exes (Serilog session log) continuously (buffered) All debug-log folders prune independently on a file-count cap of 200; when a save finds the folder over the cap, the oldest files are deleted down to the newest 100 (half the cap), so the prune fires rarely rather than on every save. Local application data — not Documents — is deliberate: Documents redirects to OneDrive, whose sync locks capture files and contends with snapshot IO under connect/close churn. Client log — AAComm.Services.Diagnostics.AACommDebugLog Static, process-wide, shared by every CommAPI instance in the process. Line format and identity tags HH:mm:ss.fff [api#N/conn#M] text api#N — the CommAPI instance, numbered in construction order (assigned in the designated constructor every overload funnels into). conn#M — that instance's successive successful channel opens. Before the first open the tag is just api#N. The connect line is the one line whose tag also carries the endpoint: [api#1/conn#1→Ethernet 172.1.1.101:5000]. Every later line is tag-only, so a reader greps the endpoint once and then follows the short tag. The ring's first entry is a one-time header: === AAComm diagnostic log — process <name> (PID <pid>), path <exe path>, AAComm <version>, started <timestamp> === Recorded events Event Line (shape) Construction CommAPI constructed Channel open (per successful open, incl. test opens) channel open (local 127.0.0.1:54321), ServerCompat=Current — the tag carries the endpoint; local is the client→AACS socket's local end, the join key (see below) TestConnection / Connect / ConnectSilent outcome Connect(Ethernet 172.1.1.101:5000) → Success in 812 ms, ServerCompat=Current — result, elapsed, endpoint, and the compat the attempt classified (captured before teardown can reset it; TestConnection always tears down before this line is written) Sync phase-1 expiry (queue abandon, no teardown) sync phase-1 expiry: abandoned in queue after 203 ms (queued-behind-live budget, TimeoutMs=100): "APos" — the budget branch is queued-behind-live (TimeoutMs + 100) or idle+starvation (TimeoutMs + 5000) Sync phase-2 expiry (teardown) sync phase-2 expiry: no reply 402 ms after dispatch at 14:03:07.101 (budget TimeoutMs 100 + 100 + grace 200 = 400 ms): "APos" → teardown — message text truncated to 64 chars. This line is what discriminates phase-1 vs phase-2 in the field Server FATAL frame received server FATAL received: <content> (ASCII and binary pipelines both) Any comms error / FATAL reaching teardown comms error/FATAL: <message> → teardown (the funnel — covers socket death paths that never produce a FATAL frame) Disconnect disconnect (<reason>) — explicit, sync-timeout, fatal, close-server, test-connection complete, or connect failed: <ConnectResult> Flush-on-severity A library in the customer's process has no reliable exit hook, so severity is the flush trigger. Ring: 10 000 entries, oldest 10 % evicted on overflow. Triggers: sync phase-2 teardown (SyncTimeout), FATAL / comms error (Fatal), and the public on-demand AACommDebugLog.Flush() (Flush, synchronous). File: {yyyy_MM_dd_HH-mm-ss}_{process}_{pid}_{trigger}.log — a snapshot of the ring, which is not cleared, so successive snapshots overlap and logging continues. Off the hot path: severity snapshots are written on the ThreadPool; the file path (directory included) is resolved at trigger time, so a concurrent directory change cannot redirect the write or its prune. Debounce: 5 s — multiple severe events inside the window produce one file (a phase-2 teardown and the FATAL it provokes do not double-write). Host bridge — AACommDebugLog.Sink Action<string, string> (source, formatted line): every event line is mirrored to it synchronously, source = the line's identity tag (the connect line's tag carries →endpoint, so hosts routing on source should prefix-match; the one-time header is ring-only). Mirrors GlobalLogger.GlobalDebugLog on the server side; hosts use it to fold AAComm diagnostics into their own session log. Sink and Flush() are the only public surface. Server log — AACommServerCore.GlobalLogger Same mechanics (the ring/file core is one source file, owned by AAComm and compiled into AACommServerCore as a linked source — separate assemblies, separate state, so a chatty client can never evict server entries), different policy: Line format: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss [Debug|Fault|UnhandledException] <source> : <message>. Files in AACommServer_DebugLogs\: {stamp}_Debug.log (the once-on-shutdown save), {stamp}_Flush.log (on-demand snapshot — the client's fire-and-forget CommAPI.FlushDebugLog() verb or the server UI), {stamp}_ImplicitShutdown.log (the abnormal last-client-death save). GlobalDebugLog feeds the server UI's live debug list; LogDebug lines land in both the UI list and the ring. Joining the two logs AACommServer identifies clients only by UserId; the client never learns its UserId. The join key is the client→AACS TCP socket, which both sides see from opposite ends: Client side — the connect line logs the socket's local end: 14:02:59.310 [api#1/conn#1→Ethernet 172.1.1.101:5000] channel open (local 127.0.0.1:54321), ServerCompat=Current Server side — on every client Open, one debug line binds UserId to the socket's remote end (the same address:port): 2026-08-24 14:02:59 [Debug] OnAACommRequest() UserId=7 : Open request for 'ET_172.1.1.101' from client endpoint 127.0.0.1:54321 Procedure, starting from either side: In the client snapshot, find the channel open line for the session of interest → take the local endpoint (127.0.0.1:54321). Grep the server's debug log for that endpoint → the line names the UserId (7). Filter the server log by UserId=7 — every server-side event for that client (malformed frames, tx overflow, implicit-shutdown bookkeeping) now correlates with the client's api#N/conn#M timeline. The reverse direction starts from a UserId and greps the endpoint in the client snapshots. Caveats: ephemeral ports are unique per live connection but recycle over time — on long-uptime machines disambiguate by timestamp proximity; each reconnect is a new conn#M and a new local port, so the join is per-connection, not per-process. Worked example — attributing a sync-timeout teardown The failure this layer exists for: an application reports "AAComm disconnected", the server log shows only an unexplained client close. With the snapshots: 14:03:06.694 [api#1/conn#1] sync phase-2 expiry: no reply 402 ms after dispatch at 14:03:06.291 (budget TimeoutMs 100 + 100 + grace 200 = 400 ms): "APos" → teardown 14:03:06.697 [api#1/conn#1] disconnect (sync-timeout) tells support: the message reached the wire (phase 2, not a queue abandon), the full grace was spent, the client — not the controller protocol — initiated the close, and the {...}_SyncTimeout.log filename alone already names the trigger. The join procedure then locates the same seconds in the server log under the bound UserId to see what the server observed (e.g. queueing behind another client's long operation). Known limitations The header's process path is best-effort (Process.MainModule can be inaccessible under permission/bitness constraints; the header then says unknown). The client ring is process-global: snapshots interleave all CommAPI instances (that is what the api#N tag is for). File IO failures are silently swallowed on the client (a diagnostic must never take the host down); the server side falls back to the Windows Event Log as before. The local-port half of the join key is available only from the real socket-backed transports; test doubles log the connect line without it.

articles/architecture/floating-point.htm.title: Floating Point Resolution | Agito AAComm SDK
articles/architecture/floating-point.htm.summary: AAComm Floating-Point Resolution Principle Data that leaves AAComm via the Extension classes (e.g., RecordingDataContainer, LoggerDataContainer, ScopeDataContainer, AllStatInterpreter) is properly resolved and ready to use. Raw IEEE 754 bit-pattern resolution is handled transparently by these classes. Limitation: Resolution only applies when data is obtained through the Extension mechanism, or for protocols that have Rx-path resolution (see below). If an unsupported upload command is issued directly via CommAPI.Send() — such as from PCSuite Terminal — the raw response is not resolved. The consumer receives unprocessed bit-masked values. ConFltSnapVal and ProgSnapVal cannot be auto-resolved via an Extension mechanism because the snapshot source parameters (ConFltSnapSrc / ProgSnapSrc) are user-configurable — the parameter types are unknown until the CCC sources are queried at runtime. TODO: Consider an Extension-level auto-resolve path for protocols currently resolved only by PCSuite UI code (ConFltSnapVal, ProgSnapVal). This would require querying snapshot source CCCs as part of the Extension flow. Resolution Core logic lives in FloatHelper (AAComm.Services) — public static class, callable directly by all consumers. FloatHelper.ResolveFloatingPoint(MessageData md, long val, bool doubleSupported, bool floatSupport) determines the correct conversion based on the parameter's MessageData type: float/double with doubleSupported — LongToDouble() (64-bit IEEE 754) float with !doubleSupported and floatSupport — IntToFloat() (32-bit IEEE 754) float with !doubleSupported and !floatSupport — returned as-is (float hole protection) int / long — returned as-is null metadata (unknown parameter) — returned as-is (safe fallback) FloatHelper.ResolveFromCCC(int ccc, long rawVal, IMessagesContainer dataContainer, bool doubleSupported, bool floatSupport) resolves via Complex CAN Code: parses CCC -> looks up MessageData -> delegates to ResolveFloatingPoint. Throws FormatException on NaN or Infinity. Float Hole Protection AllStat_64bit protocols (AllStat, Logger, Scope, ConFltSnap, ProgSnap) never transmit 32-bit float bit patterns. They either send raw integers or 64-bit doubles. These protocols pass floatSupport: false, which blocks the IntToFloat path and prevents garbage values when doubleSupported=false and a parameter has float metadata. RecUpload and ParamAbout pass floatSupport: true. Firmware-Side UserUnits (Recording Header) The per-vector UserUnits integer stored in the recording header (VectorDataContainer.UserUnits, read from GetUserUnitsIndex(i)) is part of a parallel firmware-level scaling system. It is mutually exclusive with the PCSuite UU feature at the firmware level. This value is preserved as metadata in RecParamHeader and AGF files but is NOT used for PCSuite UU scaling. PCSuite UU factors are looked up dynamically via CommAPI.GetUserUnitsEnabled() + ControllerMessagesContainer.TryGetUserUnitAxis() through the centralized FloatHelper.ApplyUserUnits() method. Double Support Flags Two independent flags control double support for different protocol groups: Flag Source Protocols Features_01.DoublePhase_1_Supported Identity[26] bit 28 RecUpload Features_02.AllStat_64bit_Supported Identity[62] bit 3 AllStat, LoggerUpload, ScopeUpload, ParamAbout, ConFltSnapVal, ProgSnapVal Protocols Protocol Container doubleSupported floatSupport Auto-resolved Rx-path resolved UU-scaled RecUpload RecordingDataContainer DoublePhase_1_Supported true Yes No Yes (ApplyUserUnits in ReadRecParamsData) LoggerUpload LoggerDataContainer AllStat_64bit_Supported false Yes No Yes (via PacketDataParser) ScopeUpload ScopeDataContainer AllStat_64bit_Supported false Yes No Yes (via PacketDataParser) AllStat AllStatInterpreter AllStat_64bit_Supported false Yes Yes Yes (ApplyUserUnits in Resolve) ParamAbout FloatHelper.ResolveParamAbout AllStat_64bit_Supported true Yes (inline) Yes Yes (via ConvertReplyToFloatIfNeed factor) ConFltSnapVal PCSuite FaultDataView AllStat_64bit_Supported false No (PCSuite UI) No Yes (PCSuite FaultDataView) ProgSnapVal PCSuite UPDataView AllStat_64bit_Supported false No (PCSuite UI) No Yes (PCSuite UPDataView) LoggerUpload / ScopeUpload Both use PacketDataParser for the common wire format: nPackets, [header, val1, val2, ...], ..., 0. Header is packet ID (Logger) or Time (Scope). Resolution is applied per value using the caller-provided MessageData list. PCSuite adapts these containers into its UI models. The CSV import path in LoggerData bypasses AAComm resolution (values are already resolved in the file). AllStat AllStatInterpreter requires a connected CommAPI (constructor delegates validation to RecParamsResolver.ValidateAPI). Every field in AllStatAxisData is resolved via mnemonic lookup against the controller's MessagesContainer — float/double fields get bit-pattern conversion, integer fields pass through as double. Rx-Path Resolution (ConvertReplyToFloatIfNeed) FloatHelper.ConvertReplyToFloatIfNeed is the inline Rx-path resolver for all message replies. It intercepts raw controller replies before delivery to the caller and converts IEEE 754 bit patterns to floating-point values. This ensures that even low-level SendReceive() consumers (e.g., PCSuite Terminal) receive properly resolved data. Resolved in the Rx path: Single-value parameters: float (IntToFloat) and double (LongToDouble) based on MessageData type. Note: the single-value path dispatches purely on MessageData.IsFloat/IsDouble — it does NOT check the doubleSupported/floatSupport flags. ParamAbout: multi-value State,MIN,MAX,DEFAULT — delegated to FloatHelper.ResolveParamAbout AllStat: multi-value comma-separated longs per axis/group — delegated to AllStatInterpreter.ResolveRawReply. Uses the static mnemonic arrays and the private Resolve() instance method to convert each value in group order. Returns reply unchanged if !AllStat_64bit_Supported. NOT resolved in the Rx path (CAN code unknown at Rx flow time): RecUpload: not resolved here — RecordingDataContainer parses raw longs and resolves per-vector with the correct feature flags. Rx-path resolution would double-convert (long→string→long parse failure) RecUploadNext: sequential packet protocol — the CAN codes are not embedded in the N2 data packets ScopeUpload / LoggerUpload: the CAN codes are supplied by the caller, not present in the reply ConFltSnapVal / ProgSnapVal: snapshot source CCCs are user-configurable and unknown without runtime query Error Handling AAComm throws generic FormatException on invalid floating-point values (NaN, Infinity). Consumer applications (e.g., PCSuite) catch and localize these messages.

AAComm Architecture Client-side communication library for sending commands to hardware controllers via AACommServer. Architecture Overview AAComm is a client library that provides a high-level API for user applications to communicate with hardware controllers. It manages the connection to AACommServer, queues messages, handles responses, and maintains controller state information. Communication Pipeline The following diagram illustrates the bidirectional communication flow between user applications and AACommServer. Note: Send and SendReceive use independent FIFO pipelines sharing a single underlying wire. Each path has its own queue (Channel), its own dispatcher task, and its own in-flight slot. Ordinary messages in the two flows do not gate each other — a long-running async Send callback does not block a concurrent SendReceive, and a SendReceive parked on its safety-net wait does not block subsequent Sends. Async Reset is the deliberate exception: later dispatch is parked until reset recovery completes. Per-flow FIFO is preserved (consecutive Sends fire callbacks in order; consecutive SRs return in order); cross-flow ordering is NOT guaranteed (an async Send and a sync SendReceive issued back-to-back may dispatch in either order). Wire writes from the two dispatchers are serialized by an internal mutex, and each dispatched message is stamped with a session-scoped correlation id (carried on the binary wire; the ASCII handler ignores it). On the binary protocol the server echoes the id on the routed reply and the receiver routes by identity (Session.TryTakeInFlight); an id of 0 — the string protocol or a legacy binary server — falls back to wire-arrival-order routing via the _wireOrder queue (safe because AACommServer processes one message per channel at a time, answers server-internal IA: queries through the same per-channel FIFO, and each client socket has a single ordered writer — so replies arrive in send order). For replies, the receiver thread hands the parsed args to the originating flow's dispatcher via a per-iteration TaskCompletionSource, and the dispatcher runs the user callback on its own thread — the receiver thread does not invoke OnReplyReceived. For push messages, the receiver hands the parsed payload to the OnPushMessageReceived event via Task.Run, so user code runs on the ThreadPool, not the receiver thread. The one exception is OnCommsError: it is invoked synchronously on the receiver thread, and long-running work in that handler will stall reply / push classification until it returns (after a fatal the session is being torn down anyway, but handlers that need to dispatch onto a UI thread should off-load with Task.Run). This receiver-never-blocks-on- reply-callbacks discipline is what unblocks the bug where an async Send callback parked on a UI dispatcher would deadlock a concurrent SendReceive from the UI thread. SendReceive is implemented on top of the sync pipeline: it builds a tagged duplicate of the user's message (IsSyncRequest = true), installs an internal wait-handle hook as OnReplyReceived, and blocks until the reply arrives or the safety-net timeout expires. The per-message IsSyncRequest marker drives event-suppression (OnCommsError and the long-operation events OnLongOperationStarted/OnLongOperationEnded are not raised for sync requests; the Reset recovery sleep is skipped). graph TB subgraph "User Application" App[Application Code] end subgraph "AAComm Library" subgraph "Public API Layer" API[CommAPI
